newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales soar in October - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales soar in October - CBI.

text.p: British retail sales soared to an eight-year high in October, having eased off in September, the Confederation of British Industry said on Friday.

The CBI's distributive trades survey showed that a positive balance of 55 percent of retailers saw higher sales last month. Sixty-seven percent of the 15,000 outlets surveyed said sales rose, while only 12 percent saw sales fall.

The balance of retailers reporting higher sales volumes in October overshot expectations, rising to the highest level since August 1988. Retailers said business was above average for the time of year and more so than at any time since November 1988.
A balance of 43 percent of British retailers said orders placed with suppliers rose last month, the sharpest rate of increase since January 1988.
But stocks appear to be on the increase again, with more firms reporting excess stocks than at any time in the last year.
"For the first time since January 1990, all sectors within retailing have experienced some sales growth," said Alastair Eperon, chairman of the CBI's distributive trades survey panel.
He said the three-month moving average of underlying sales growth also strengthened in October, suggesting consumer confidence held up, but the pattern of sales remained uneven.
Wholesalers' volumes grew a little more slowly in October although the slowdown was less than had been expected, the CBI said. But stocks were run down and sales are expected to pick up in November.
Motor traders reported another small rise in annual sales even though a fall had been expected. But business was considered to be below average for the time of year, for the first time since May.
Retail sectors most closely linked to the housing market, such as furniture and carpets, durable household goods and china, continued to enjoy strong sales growth, the CBI said.
Clothing, leather and footwear retailers also saw sales growth pick up and off-licences benefited from the first rise in volumes since June.
Grocers again reported strong sales increases and confectioners revelled in the strongest rise in sales they had seen since April 1992.
The 15,000 retail outlets canvassed are responsible for about 40 percent of employment in the retailing, wholesale and motor trades.
